biography: Ciro Aliperti Jr. wasn't born into racing royalty, but his childhood in the shadow of Interlagos certainly fueled his ambition. His father, a mechanic for a local karting team, instilled a love for speed early on. Ciro spent his formative years dismantling and rebuilding engines, learning the intricate dance between man and machine. One sweltering afternoon, when a driver called in sick, 12-year-old Ciro seized his chance, piloting the kart to an unexpected victory. The taste of victory was intoxicating, and he dedicated himself to mastering the craft. His ascent through the Brazilian racing ranks was steady, punctuated by a dominant season in Formula Vee. Now, at 24, Ciro finds himself piloting the MetalMoro MRX Honda P3, a proving ground for endurance racing talent. He's hungry to prove he belongs on the world stage, one calculated maneuver at a time.
drivingStyle: Aliperti is a calculating driver, known for his strategic approach rather than outright aggression. He meticulously analyzes track conditions and rival tendencies, conserving his tires and energy for a late-race surge. He favors smooth, precise lines through corners, minimizing wheelspin and maximizing exit speed. While not the flashiest driver on the grid, Aliperti possesses a remarkable ability to maintain composure under pressure, often capitalizing on the mistakes of his more impetuous competitors. His tire management is considered exceptional, allowing him to push harder for longer stints than most.

rivalries.reason: A fierce on-track battle in Formula Vee that resulted in a controversial penalty call against Aliperti, costing him the championship.
Monteiro's aggressive driving style clashes directly with Aliperti's calculated approach, leading to several close calls and heated exchanges.
Tanaka is considered a protege and prodigy, which Aliperti deeply resents as Aliperti has worked hard for his position.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of worn-out racing gloves, believing they bring him good fortune.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba song before every race to calm his nerves and center his focus.
Refuses to eat anything red on race day, citing a childhood superstition about red cars crashing.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about brute force; it's about understanding the equation and solving it before anyone else."
careerHighlight: Winning the Formula Vee championship after a season-long battle, showcasing his strategic driving and tire management skills.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Brazilian Endurance Championship, a mistake he attributes to overconfidence.
